To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adaptation of the robot gripper orientation to the payload shape can lead to gentle handling processes with minimized undesired shear forces.

1) the shear forces on grasped objects can be reduced to zero by adapting the gripper orientation, 2) the shear force reduction is independent of the payload's shape, 3) the shear force is reduced by the square of the payload's width and 4) the shear force depends only on the payload's mass.
we have developed a novel methodology for gentle robot handling of grasped objects, which we have implemented and tested in a real industrial robot cell.
